questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Mark the correct statements (s).
(i) Manganese exhibits +7 oxidation state
(ii) Zinc forms coloured ions
(iii) [CoF6]3- is diamagnetic
(iv) Sc forms +4 oxidation state
(v) Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state
questions.solution:
Outer electronic configuration of Mn is 3d54s2 which means it exhibits +7 oxidation state
Zinc does not form coloured ions as it has completely filled 3d104s2 configuration.
In [CoF6]3-,Co3+ is a d7 system. Fluoride is a weak field ligand and hence it can not cause pairing of electrons.

Sc can form a maximum of +3 oxidation state as it has an outer electronic configuration of 3d14s2 .
Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state as this O.S. is the most stable one for it.
Hence i, v are correct while ii,iii,iv are incorrect.

questions.solution:
Writing the balanced oxidation and reduction half-reactions, making the number of electrons same in them and adding both half-reactions gives us the final balanced equation:

[Fe2++C2O42−  →  Fe3++2CO2+3e−]×2 (oxidation)

Cr2O72−+14H++6e−  →  2Cr3++7H2O (reduction)

On adding both the reactions, we get,

Cr2O72−+2Fe2++2C2O42−+14H+→2Cr3++2Fe3++4CO2+7H2O

Thus, 6 electrons are donated from oxidized substances to the reduced substance.

questions.q: What is the possible product of the reaction in which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mole</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>HNO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> is reduced by absorption of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>moles</mi></math> electrons?
questions.solution:
Here, when nitric acid is converted into any of the nitrogen compound, the oxidation state of nitrogen is changed and for oxygen and hydrogen, it remains unchanged.

Let the oxidation state of Nitrogen in HNO3 be x.

Then, +1+x+3-2=0⇒x-5=0⇒x=+5.

Now, after absorption of 4 moles of electrons, the oxidation state of nitrogen will become

N5++4e-→N+

Out of the given compounds, the compound having the oxidation state of nitrogen as +1 is N2O.

Thus, here nitric acid is getting converted into dinitrogen oxide.

1 mole of HNO3→givesx moles of N2O

Applying principle of atom conservation for nitrogen,

1×moles of HNO3=2×moles of N2O1×1=2xx=12=0.5 mol
